svg.title: Known versus unknown supply chain threats: which control sees which
svg.text: Known versus unknown: what each control can see
A vulnerability database only knows what someone already reported. Malicious updates and backdoors are new by definition.
KNOWN problems
A CVE, advisory or malware report already exists
Detected by
- SCA and SBOM matching (OSV, NVD, GHSA)
- container image scanners (Trivy, Grype)
- KEV and EPSS to rank what to fix first
- malware feeds of already-reported packages
Examples
- Struts CVE-2017-5638 (Equifax): patch existed
- an old lodash or minimist with a published CVE
Weakness: lag between the attack and the report;
a clean scan says "no known issue", not "safe".
UNKNOWN problems
Nobody has reported it yet (zero-day or fresh malice)
Detected (sometimes) by
- behaviour: install-time network, new processes
- malicious-package heuristics (GuardDog-style)
- provenance and reproducible-build comparison
- diffing releases, maintainer and ownership changes
Examples
- xz-utils backdoor: release tarball differed
from the git source; found by a performance anomaly
- Shai-Hulud worm: new versions of trusted packages
Defence: shrink exposure (cooldown on new versions,
pinning, least privilege) and detect early.
